articles.title: Doodhi Halwa: How to Make the Classic Bottle Gourd Dessert Without Khoya
articles.excerpt: This simplified Punjabi recipe turns a humble lauki into a rich, cardamom-scented halwa in under 45 minutes — no specialty ingredients required.
articles.image_caption: A serving of doodhi halwa garnished with chopped nuts and saffron strands. The traditional Punjabi dessert is made from grated bottle gourd slow-cooked with milk, sugar, and cardamom.
articles.nri_angle: Bottle gourd is increasingly available at Indian grocery stores and mainstream supermarkets in the US, UK, and Canada, making doodhi halwa an accessible traditional dessert for diaspora families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Story of South Indian Filter Coffee: From Smuggled Beans to a Global Morning Ritual
articles.excerpt: How seven coffee beans smuggled from Yemen in the 17th century gave rise to India's most beloved brewing tradition and a cultural identity that travels with the diaspora.
articles.image_caption: A traditional South Indian steel coffee filter used to brew decoction by slow drip. The two-chambered device has been the heart of filter kaapi culture across Tamil Nadu and Karnataka for over a century.
articles.nri_angle: Filter kaapi has followed the South Indian diaspora worldwide, with the steel filter and tumbler-dabara remaining essential items in NRI kitchens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six Simple Tests to Check If Your Paneer Is Real or Fake at Home
articles.excerpt: As India cracks down on synthetic dairy products, FSSAI-backed tests using iodine, warm water, and a hot pan can help consumers identify adulterated paneer before it reaches their plate.
articles.nri_angle: Paneer quality and food safety is a universal concern for Indian households worldwide, particularly for diaspora families who rely on it as a primary protein source and often purchase from specialty stores where provenance is harder to verify
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kanwar Yatra Camps Blend Tradition and Street Food With 7,000 Rotis a Day
articles.excerpt: Volunteer camps along the Uttar Pradesh pilgrimage route serve everything from shahi paneer and dal makhani to pizza, momos, and pasta — all prepared without onion and garlic.
articles.image_caption: Kanwar Yatris carry holy water from the Ganges during the annual pilgrimage. Food camps along the route serve thousands of rotis and traditional street food daily.
articles.nri_angle: The Kanwar Yatra is one of India's most iconic religious pilgrimages, and its evolving food culture reflects the broader fusion of tradition and modernity that resonates with the diaspora
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian Bars Crack Asia's 50 Best List as Goa's Boilermaker Storms Into Top 10
articles.excerpt: Boilermaker in Goa jumped 22 places to No. 8, while Bengaluru's SOKA and Bar Spirit Forward reinforced the city's growing reputation as India's cocktail capital.
articles.image_caption: The interior of Boilermaker in Siolim, Goa. The bar jumped 22 places to No. 8 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 and was named Best Bar in India.
articles.nri_angle: India's growing presence on the global cocktail stage is a point of pride for NRIs, many of whom visit these bars when traveling home and follow the country's evolving food and drink scene.

articles.title: Nick and Joe Jonas Snack on Bhajia, Kachori, and Papad During Tour Break
articles.excerpt: The Jonas Brothers continue to embrace Indian cuisine on their 20th anniversary tour, with Nick's love for Indian food now a recurring highlight of their social media presence.
articles.nri_angle: Nick Jonas's genuine embrace of Indian food and Bollywood culture has made him a beloved figure among the Indian diaspora, turning casual snack moments into cultural touchpoints.

articles.title: Himachali Siddu: How To Make the Mountain Bread That Fueled Himalayan Shepherds
articles.excerpt: This steamed, walnut-stuffed bread from Himachal Pradesh is centuries old, protein-rich, and easy to make at home with just wheat flour, yeast, and a handful of nuts and herbs.
articles.image_caption: Siddu, a traditional steamed bread from Himachal Pradesh, is made with wheat dough stuffed with a spiced filling and cooked over a slow flame.
articles.nri_angle: Siddu uses pantry staples available worldwide, making it an accessible way for diaspora families to connect with Himachali mountain food traditions at home.

articles.title: What Made Your Thali Costlier in July: Onions, Oil, and Chicken Drive Kitchen Inflation
articles.excerpt: Home-cooked vegetarian meals rose 4% and non-vegetarian meals 9% year-on-year as onion, oil, LPG, and chicken prices surged, a Crisil report finds.
articles.nri_angle: The thali cost index is a useful barometer of food inflation for diaspora families tracking the cost of living back home in India.

articles.title: FSSAI Penalises Fortune Oil Maker AWL After Sunflower Oil Fails Vitamin D Test
articles.excerpt: India's food safety regulator has taken action against AWL Agri Business, formerly Adani Wilmar, after a Fortune sunflower oil sample did not meet mandatory Vitamin D fortification standards, part of an intensifying crackdown on food labelling and quality.
articles.nri_angle: Fortune is widely available in Indian grocery stores across the US, UK and Canada; diaspora consumers buying imported Fortune oil should check fortification labels.

articles.title: How Zorawar Kalra Built a Global Indian Restaurant Empire From His Father's Legacy
articles.excerpt: The son of legendary food critic Jiggs Kalra reveals how he recruited two of India's best young chefs to launch Masala Library — and turned Indian food into a global brand with 50 restaurants and counting.
articles.image_caption: The late Jiggs Kalra, known as the Czar of Indian cuisine, whose culinary legacy his son Zorawar has expanded into a global restaurant empire.
articles.nri_angle: Kalra's plan to open 50 restaurants across North America directly targets the Indian diaspora market, filling a gap in casual modern Indian dining that cities like New York, Toronto, and the Bay Area currently lack.

articles.title: Sweetgreen Cuts Full-Year Outlook as Cyclospora Outbreak Tanks Salad Demand
articles.excerpt: The salad chain slashed its same-store sales forecast and warned of prolonged consumer hesitancy toward fresh produce, even though none of its ingredients have been linked to the nationwide illness.
articles.image_caption: Sweetgreen shares have fallen roughly 30% over the past month as the nationwide cyclospora outbreak reduced consumer demand for salads and fresh produce. The chain cut its full-year same-store sales forecast nearly in half on Thursday.
articles.nri_angle: The cyclospora outbreak affects Indian-American consumers who frequent salad chains, while raising parallels with food safety standards in the broader restaurant industry.

articles.title: Kolkata's Iconic Flurys Opens First North India Outlet in Gurugram Ahead of Centenary
articles.excerpt: The 99-year-old tearoom brings its Park Street heritage to Galleria Market as it eyes a national footprint before its 2027 centenary.
articles.image_caption: Flurys, the iconic Kolkata tearoom on Park Street, has opened its first outlet in North India at Gurugram's Galleria Market ahead of its centenary in 2027.
articles.nri_angle: For Bengalis and Kolkata natives abroad, Flurys evokes deep nostalgia — its expansion signals that iconic local brands are scaling nationally.

articles.title: India Today Investigation Exposes Sprawling Fake Dairy Racket Across Delhi-NCR
articles.excerpt: Undercover reporting reveals synthetic paneer, adulterated milk, and fake khoya flowing into restaurants and street vendors, raising alarm about food safety enforcement gaps.
articles.nri_angle: The investigation highlights food safety risks that concern diaspora members who regularly consume dairy products during visits to India and worry about the authenticity of Indian dairy exports.

articles.title: Gujarat Bans Analogue Paneer and Dairy Substitutes in Widening Food Safety Crackdown
articles.excerpt: The western Indian state joins a national push to pull cheap vegetable-fat imitations off menus and store shelves, with over 2,500 eateries inspected and hundreds of kilograms of substandard food destroyed.
articles.image_caption: Paneer, a staple of Indian cuisine, is at the centre of Gujarat's new food safety crackdown banning analogue dairy substitutes.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who regularly consume paneer should verify sourcing, especially unbranded loose products; the crackdown highlights a food safety gap in India that affects diaspora visits and imports.

articles.title: From ICRISAT Lab to Rs 2 Crore Business: The Indian Scientist Behind Edible Spoons
articles.excerpt: Narayana Peesapaty quit crop research to build Bakeys, the Hyderabad startup making cutlery from jowar, rice and wheat that you eat after your meal or let decompose in days.
articles.image_caption: Bakey's edible cutlery, invented by former ICRISAT scientist Narayana Peesapaty, offers a biodegradable alternative to single-use plastic.
articles.nri_angle: The edible cutlery movement combines Indian scientific ingenuity with global sustainability goals, exemplifying the frugal innovation model India is increasingly exporting worldwide.

articles.title: Global Food Prices Set to Surge as Iran War and El Niño Squeeze Supply Chains
articles.excerpt: The FAO's chief economist warns that commodity prices will start climbing by year-end, with a full-blown food price spike likely in 2027 as the Strait of Hormuz closure drives up energy and fertilizer costs.
articles.nri_angle: India's dependence on imported edible oils and fertilizers means rising global food costs directly pressure domestic inflation and reduce the purchasing power of remittances.

articles.title: India Ranks 13th Among World's Best Cuisines in TasteAtlas Awards
articles.excerpt: Butter garlic naan and Amritsari kulcha lead Indian entries, with Mumbai named among the world's top five food cities in the annual global food rankings.
articles.nri_angle: The TasteAtlas ranking validates Indian cuisine's global standing, resonating with diaspora communities who have long championed their food traditions abroad.

articles.title: Sysco Halts All Mexican Lettuce Purchases as Cyclosporiasis Outbreak Kills Two

articles.title: Singhara Flour Cheela: The Fasting-Friendly Pancake Worth Making Year-Round

articles.title: Mumbai, Delhi and Jaipur Ranked Among World's Best Street Food Cities
articles.excerpt: Top chefs endorse global rankings as Mumbai's khau gallis and Delhi's Mughlai lanes earn international recognition from Time Out and TasteAtlas.
articles.nri_angle: Street food serves as a visceral connection to home for the diaspora; international validation may spur more Indian street food concepts abroad.

articles.title: Maharashtra Bans Analogue Paneer for One Year, Violators Face Jail Time
articles.excerpt: The state escalates from mandatory disclosure to an outright prohibition on fake paneer in all hotels and restaurants, with penalties including six months imprisonment.

articles.excerpt: A Pakistani-born chef's home-style cooking — from charcoal tandoor naan to oxtail biryani — is winning over Hawaiʻi's food scene and its desi community.

articles.title: Bengaluru's Legendary MTR Is Opening in Sydney, Bringing Its Century-Old Dosas to Australia

articles.image_caption: Hyderabad police seized 25,000 kilograms of adulterated spices laced with industrial dyes in a crackdown on food safety violations.

articles.title: India's Food Regulator Bars Dabur From Selling Products With Misleading '100%' Claims
articles.excerpt: FSSAI issues a prohibition order against Dabur India for labeling products as '100% Natural' and '100% Pure' without valid regulatory backing.
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs regularly purchase Dabur products abroad, from honey to ghee. This ruling may force label changes on products sold in Indian grocery stores worldwide.

articles.title: FSSAI Bans Select Variants of Old Monk, Royal Challenge, and Bagpiper Over Artificial Flavouring

articles.image_caption: Old Monk rum is among the brands affected by FSSAI's ban on select variants containing artificial flavouring agents.
articles.nri_angle: Old Monk is an iconic brand among Indian diaspora communities worldwide; the ban raises questions about variants sold internationally.

articles.title: Beyond the Rasgulla War: How Sun-Dried Mango Powers Odisha's Overlooked Cuisine
articles.excerpt: Ambula — salted, sun-dried mango — quietly anchors Odia cooking, lending a sour depth to curries, chutneys, and rice dishes that most Indian food lovers have never encountered.
articles.image_caption: Sun-dried mango, or ambula, is a staple of Odia cuisine used in curries, dals, and chutneys across Odisha.
articles.nri_angle: Introduces diaspora readers to a largely unknown regional Indian cuisine and a home-preservation technique — sun-drying mango — that is accessible even abroad.

articles.title: TUA & Synthe Brings Futuristic Cocktails and Pan-Asian Cuisine to Kolkata
articles.excerpt: A new drink-and-dine destination pairs Chef Vaibhav Bhargava's Pan-Asian menu with Ankur Chawla's decade-themed cocktail programme spanning 2030 to 2110.

articles.title: Sawan Somwar Is Here: Build a Satisfying Vrat Thali Without Onion or Garlic
articles.excerpt: The holy month of Shravan is underway, and today marks the first Monday fast. Here's how to put together a complete fasting thali anchored by a rich, no-onion paneer masala.
articles.image_caption: A traditional Sawan Somwar vrat thali includes sabudana, paneer, and fruit — all permissible during the Shravan fasting period.
articles.nri_angle: Guides diaspora families on sourcing vrat-friendly ingredients like kuttu flour, sendha namak (sold as Himalayan pink salt), and samak rice abroad, with practical tips for batch-prepping fasting meals around busy weekday schedules.

articles.title: How Strangers Are Feeding India's Exam Protesters Through Swiggy and Zomato
articles.excerpt: Anonymous supporters across India and abroad are using food delivery apps to send meals to student protesters, turning digital platforms into tools of solidarity.
articles.image_caption: Anonymous supporters have been ordering food through Swiggy and Zomato for delivery to exam-protest sites across Indian cities.
articles.nri_angle: Overseas Indians are using Swiggy and Zomato to send food to protest sites, turning delivery apps into a way for the diaspora to participate in civic movements from afar.

articles.title: Six Indian Cities Crack TasteAtlas Global Top 100, Mumbai Leads at Number Five
articles.excerpt: Mumbai's street food culture propelled it into the top five of TasteAtlas's 2025-26 ranking of the world's best food cities, while Amritsar, New Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Chennai also earned spots on the 100-city list.
articles.nri_angle: The TasteAtlas ranking validates the culinary traditions diaspora communities carry with them, from Mumbai's vada pav to Chennai's filter coffee.

articles.nri_angle: The controversy highlights how diaspora-run restaurants abroad represent India's identity — and the emotional weight of accurate territorial depiction for overseas communities.

articles.title: A Japanese Chef Spent 15 Years Perfecting Biryani. Tokyo's Michelin Guide Noticed.

articles.title: Flipkart Enters Food Delivery With Low Commissions, Targeting Zomato-Swiggy Duopoly

articles.title: Beetroot Cutlet Recipe: How To Make Crispy Tikki at Home
articles.excerpt: This vibrant beetroot tikki combines grated beets, mashed potato, and Indian spices into a crispy, protein-rich snack that works as an evening nibble, party starter, or even a burger patty.
articles.nri_angle: Beetroot cutlets are a simple way for diaspora cooks to recreate a beloved Indian street snack with ingredients available at any grocery store abroad.
